thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated TLS handshake failures observed from edge euwest-1 -> internal inference gateways. 5xx rate spiked from 0.2% to 8.7% in last 3m. Affected routes: /v1/generate (hosted), /v1/embeddings (hosted).

pagerduty: Paging Ashok (network oncall) and Diane (platform oncall). Please acknowledge.

ashok: ack — I’m on it, looking at edge metrics and ELB health.

ashok: quick summary from dashboards: 502/503 originating at L7 LB -> TLS handshake errors on downstream connections to private pool. Connection error msg shows "tls: handshake failure" and a spike in TCP retransmits.

ashok: running tcpdump on gw-02 in euwest-1 to confirm MTU/path issues:```sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -n tcp port 443 -c 200``` will paste samples shortly.

ashok: tcpdump sample (trimmed):```14:23:12.123456 IP 10.4.2.5.443 > 10.10.3.8.52900: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 67890,nop,wscale 7], length 0
14:23:12.124000 IP 10.10.3.8.52900 > 10.4.2.5.443: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0, length 0``` Noting R from client-side after SYN-ACK, indicates app closed socket — suspicious.

ashok: cert rotation timeline: we rolled new intermediate cert for internal load balancer at 05:00 UTC. Rotation job reported success but there is a config commit at 05:01 that toggled TLS min-version to 1.3 only. Some older clients still negotiate 1.2. Hypothesis A: cert chain mismatch + strict TLS version caused handshake failures. Hypothesis B: MTU/path PMTU blackhole causing TLS fragments to drop -> handshake incomplete.

diane: I’m pulling control-plane logs for the LB and identity service. Also checking recent puppet/ansible commits.

sean: customer-ops-bot reported errors from a large customer with many concurrent streams — they saw high latency then 502s. Raising potential customer impact: some requests retried and hit quota.

elena: Adding network engineer oncall @oncall-nw for VPC peering checks. We had a peering update in euwest-1 yesterday to adjust route priorities.

oncall-nw: Joining. Checking VPC peering status and SG/NACL. I see no peer disconnects but there was a route change at 04:58 UTC that lowered MTU for transit ENIs to 1400. Could be related.

ashok: good catch. TLS handshake with modern stacks can include large ClientHello (SNI + ALPN + cert lists). If PMTU is 1400 and path had 1500 previously, fragmentation behavior could change. Need to test MSS/MSS clamp.

ashok: quick mitigation attempt: 1) Temporarily allow TLS min-version 1.2 on the LB config 2) revert ENI MTU change to 1500 on a small subset (gw-02) 3) enable short-term proxy fallback to alternate pool that still has old cert chain. Rolling now.

incidents-bot: config-change: LB config updated to allow TLS 1.2 — change id cfg-2026-09-12-1.

ashok: reverted MTU on gw-02 (10.4.2.5) to 1500. Monitoring.

ashok: re-running tcpdump after MTU revert:```14:28:01.223456 IP 10.10.3.8.52901 > 10.4.2.5.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:28:01.223500 IP 10.4.2.5.443 > 10.10.3.8.52901: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:28:01.223520 IP 10.10.3.8.52901 > 10.4.2.5.443: Flags [.], ack 1, win 64240, length 0``` Handshake proceeds, no R.

ashok: metrics: TLS handshake failures dropped from 8.7% -> 0.5% over 4m after MTU revert + TLS min-version rollback. So mitigation effective.

diane: taking over incident lead for postmortem. We should capture timeline, blast radius, customer impact, root cause hypothesis, and action items.

elena: timeline (rough): 04:58 UTC route/MTU change deployed; 05:00 cert rotation; 05:02 LB config tightened TLS to 1.3; 05:23 alerts firing; 05:24 paging and ack; 05:30 mitigations (tls_min rollback & MTU revert) applied; 05:34 metrics improving.

sean: customer impact: three customers reported elevated 502s, one (enterprise) saw retries that triggered rate limit events. Need to notify CS and SRE for customer callbacks and possible quota reimbursement.

ashok: hypotheses ranked: 1) MTU reduction causing TLS fragments to be dropped (supported by tcpdump and rapid fix), 2) TLS min-version strictness amplifying failures for older clients (contributed but not primary), 3) cert chain misconfiguration on rotation (ruled less likely — rotation logs show correct chain and cert validation passes in lab).

diane: Action items (initial): - network: audit recent peering/route/MTU changes and add preflight for MTU-sensitive paths (ashok, oncall-nw) - infra: add canary for TLS rotation to verify handshake end-to-end (sean, elena) - platform: rollback gating: ensure TLS config changes are staged on canaries before global (diane) - customer: outreach to affected customers with timeline and credits (cs lead)

ashok: saving command snippets used for repro and evidence:```# dump MTU on interface
ip link show dev eth0
# revert mtu
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500
# LB tls config check
curl -sS https://lb-ctrl.local/config | jq '.tls.min_version'```

elena: adding a note: we also saw increased TCP retransmit counters on the path prior to detection; we should wire that into alerting to catch PMTU regressions faster.

incidents-bot: Incident severity set to sev2. Title omitted per Slack thread rules.

diane: I’ll start the in-incident RCA doc and invite network/infra to the doc. Please paste any logs or additional artifacts here. We’ll follow up with a formal postmortem with root cause and timeline.

ashok: attaching sample LB auth logs (trimmed):```[2026-09-12T05:21:11Z] connection from 10.10.3.8:52900 - tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure
[2026-09-12T05:21:13Z] connection from 10.10.3.9:52902 - tls handshake failed: write: connection reset by peer```

sean: noting downstream effect: customer-facing SDKs that pinned TLS 1.2 bundles probably recovered once TLS min-version rollback happened. Recommend documenting supported TLS versions and testing on upgrade paths.

diane: Good. For the postmortem: include root cause statement: "A recent route update lowered MTU on transit ENIs, which caused TLS handshake packets to be dropped; a concurrent tightening of LB TLS policy to 1.3 increased failure symptoms for some clients. Combined, these caused elevated 5xx rates until MTU and TLS policy were reverted."

oncall-nw: I will run a full sweep across euwest-1 and verify no other gateways have the 1400 MTU. Also will restore automated MTU check in our predeploy pipeline.

diane: thanks team. closing alert channel once postmortem doc is linked. If anyone has remaining logs, paste them here.

customer-ops-bot: Noted — CS lead assigned, outreach scheduled for impacted customers at 07:00 UTC."
